rule: logical = at least one example task's answer changed. noise = at least one touched example, all touched examples unchanged, no prior change that moved an outcome. ambiguous = no example shows a change and no touched example proves nothing changed, or the evidence is mixed (for example touched and unchanged examples but a prior similar change that moved an outcome, or conflicting priors, or only one thin untouched example, or partial coverage).

H3-N1.why: Calendar colour changes, but the checker ignores colour. Both touched examples keep the same answer.

H3-N2.why: File names gain spaces, but the checker treats underscores and spaces as the same. Both touched examples keep the same answer.

H3-L1.why: Password length goes from 8 to 12. The 10-character example flips from solved to NOT solved.

H3-L2.why: Reminders must now be before the event. The after-the-event example flips from solved to NOT solved.

H3-N3.why: Search results are sorted by relevance, but the checker ignores order. Both touched examples keep the same answer. The prior is noise from the H3-N1 run.

H3-L3.why: The text says clarification, but a note must now have a title. The no-title example flips from solved to NOT solved. The noise prior is misleading.

H3-A1.why: Text may switch to Spanish, but the only example is a count, not text, and untouched. Thin evidence, proves nothing either way.

H3-A2.why: Images may switch to thumbnails, but both examples are names and titles, untouched. The priors conflict, one noise and one logical, both from real earlier runs in this test.

H3-A3.why: Only Spotify changes, Venmo does not. The Spotify example is touched and unchanged, the Venmo example is untouched. Partial coverage, proves nothing about Spotify titles.

H3-A4.why: Two touched examples are unchanged, which points to noise, but a prior similar password change, H3-L1, moved an outcome. Mixed evidence, so hold.
